title: Self-sustaining acceleration conditions -- software-only, economic feedback with no software-only before or during it, and neither, each by four dates

source.wave: self-sustaining acceleration (Cunningham et al., "The Economics of Recursive Self-Improvement" (July 2026)), min duration 6 months

conditioning.definitions:
Definitions. These follow the framework in Cunningham et al., "The Economics of Recursive Self-Improvement" (July 2026).
Algorithmic efficiency: the inverse of the training compute needed to reach a given level of AI capability. Self-sustaining acceleration: its growth becomes self-accelerating -- as algorithmic efficiency rises, its growth rate also rises.

Software-only self-sustaining acceleration. Hold fixed the number of human researchers, all compute (for training, experiments and AI inference used in research) and data. The condition holds if, even so, a 1% rise in algorithmic efficiency raises the rate of new algorithmic improvements by more than 1%. This counts both the direct effect of existing ideas on finding new ones and the indirect effect of better AI models doing research.
Formally: ε(Ȧ,A) + ε(Ȧ,C)·ε(C,A) > 1, where C is AI capability, Ȧ is algorithmic improvements and A is algorithmic efficiency.

Self-sustaining acceleration with economic feedback. Hold fixed only the number of human researchers. Compute and data may grow, but only to the extent that resources generated by AI capability gains pay for that growth. Those resources are revenue from better models, or financing that responds to capability progress. Each such input is assumed to grow in proportion to those resources. The condition holds if this whole system accelerates: the growth rates of algorithmic efficiency and of these capability-funded inputs rise as their levels rise. Growth in compute that would have happened anyway does not count.
Formally: the dominant eigenvalue of the matrix of elasticities of each stock's growth with respect to each stock (algorithmic efficiency, training compute, experimental compute, research-inference compute, data) exceeds 1.

A one-off jump in compute, from hype, new funding or anything else, does not satisfy either condition. The conditions concern how strongly progress feeds back into itself, not how fast it moves.
conditioning.instruction: Every condition stands alone: each names one kind of acceleration and one date, and is not combined with any other condition. Treat each condition as a fact about the world -- whether or not anyone has measured or announced it -- and not as an intervention: update your expectations about everything that would ordinarily accompany it -- investment, compute, the pace of AI capability progress, deployment, and how governments and developers respond -- and then forecast each question in that world. Do not hold other factors fixed where the condition would change them. The definitions hold some inputs fixed only to say what each condition is; they do not assume that those inputs stay fixed in the world you forecast. No policy condition applies: as in the unconditional forecast, assume whatever AI policies you expect to be implemented.
conditioning.unconditional_forecast: forecast the world as you expect it to unfold, including whatever AI progress, and whatever self-sustaining acceleration, you expect.

groups.heading: SOFTWARE-ONLY ACCELERATION CONDITIONS
groups.instruction: For each condition below, assume that software-only self-sustaining acceleration holds without a break for at least 6 months, over a period that lies entirely between today and the condition's date.
groups.assumption: These conditions assume nothing about self-sustaining acceleration with economic feedback beyond what software-only acceleration implies.
groups.horizon: each condition's period ends no later than its date: December 31 of 2027, 2028, 2030 or 2040.

source.wave: self-sustaining acceleration (Cunningham et al., "The Economics of Recursive Self-Improvement" (July 2026)), min duration 6 months

groups.heading: ECONOMIC-FEEDBACK ACCELERATION CONDITIONS
groups.instruction: For each condition below, assume that self-sustaining acceleration with economic feedback holds without a break for at least 6 months, over a period that lies entirely between today and the condition's date.
groups.assumption: In every condition in this section, software-only self-sustaining acceleration does not hold at any point within that period or before it. Whether it holds after that period is left open.
groups.horizon: each condition's period ends no later than its date: December 31 of 2027, 2028, 2030 or 2040.

source.wave: self-sustaining acceleration (Cunningham et al., "The Economics of Recursive Self-Improvement" (July 2026)), min duration 6 months

groups.heading: NO-ACCELERATION CONDITIONS
groups.instruction: For each condition below, assume that by the condition's date neither holds: no condition in the software-only section and no condition in the economic-feedback section.
groups.assumption: AI progress may still be fast in these conditions, and either kind of acceleration may hold for shorter spells; only the two conditions above, as stated, are ruled out.
groups.horizon: each condition's period ends no later than its date: December 31 of 2027, 2028, 2030 or 2040.

notes.design: 2026-11-18: P(cat | S), P(cat | F) and P(cat | neither) at each date; the separate elicitation call (data/acceleration_elicit.json) asks P(S) and P(F) in the same words. S and F can both hold (F, then S after F's period), so the three do not partition the outcomes.
notes.today: Periods run from 'today', the prompt's first line, so the set is the same file on every run date.
